lessons_for_next_section: A one-clause compose-by-name pointer has nowhere to go in a contract.shapes row: name is the only prose field the shape renderer prints and the compose-by-name checker does not read it. Where a shape shares an (id, quote) pair with a builds_on skill, re-anchor the shape to the sentence of the record its own schema actually encodes instead of hunting for a field to put the pointer in.

A restate-and-extend warning is not always an uncited claim: F-b5-01's second sentence already said what cap-state-persistence's extension said, so the fix was a better quote, not a new proposed row. Read the whole cited record before splitting a row - the missing evidence is sometimes in the half of the paragraph the quote left out.

The 3-10 invariant and 6-10 instruction budgets make 'split the row' unavailable in exactly the skills that need it most: cap-provenance, cap-state-persistence and cap-tool-access were all at a ceiling. The two moves that work at a ceiling are labelling the extension proposed inside the row (cap-state-persistence-implement instructions[4] is the worked example) and deleting an extension a sibling row already carries.

Lesson 59's prose-criterion defect did not stop at the build layer: six of the thirteen capability-interface skills carried the same shape. A lessons row closes a defect only after the sweep reaches every layer that shares it, not the layer that surfaced it.
